name: Root Holes, Contraction Repair, and Punctured Subcubes
statement: For a finite well-graded family and present state $R$, deletion of coordinate $e$ makes the projected state a valid root exactly when every missing rooted union has its $e$-neighbor present. If the family is also union closed and a missing state $W$ has present neighbors in every coordinate of $C$, then the entire coordinate $C$-subcube through $W$, except $W$ itself, is present; hence the family has at least $2^{|C|}-1$ states.
proof: Rooted union commutes with coordinate deletion, while a missing state appears after deletion precisely when its coordinate neighbor is present. Pairwise neighbor states force all two-coordinate flips by well-gradedness, and union closure then generates every nonempty flip set.
